task_retrieval_key:
A woman in her 70s with a history of recurrent stasis dermatitis treated with long-term topical and systemic corticosteroids presented to the clinic with painful swelling over the right lower leg of 1 week's duration. She recalled being traumatized by plants on her right lower leg 3 months before presentation. She grew plants, especially orchids, inside her bedroom and on the balcony.
There were necrotic ulcers covered by hemorrhagic crusts and purulent debris on the right lower leg. She was afebrile.
